subject: Post-call: Migration interoperability signals & next test plan
messages:
From: Josh Park <josh@stellarmedia.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Zhao <anita@stellarmedia.com>
Date: 2027-07-31T17:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up & clarifications from today's migration discovery

Thanks Grace — good conversation today. Short recap from our side and a few clarifying asks so your team can scope the POC: 

1) Goals: evaluate how close we can swap our current hyperscaler endpoints to Redwood with minimal prompt changes and no regression in quality for our editorial assistant (mostly short completion + few-shot prompts). We also need to validate streaming behavior for live typing UI.

2) Priority tests we'd like Redwood to run (or help us run):
  - API surface and param mapping: OpenAI-compatible endpoint parity (errors, function-calling, stop sequences, streaming frames).
  - Prompt diff: token-level output deltas on 50 canonical prompts (we'll share).
  - Latency tail and burst: 95/99 p50/p95 for typical 1-2k token sessions during peak traffic.
  - Sanity on caching/kv semantics: does prefix caching affect role/stop handling?

3) Constraints: We cannot share production PII; tests must run on synthetic data or sanitized samples. We have a hard date for a decision around the end of August, so a 2-week technical POC is preferred.

Ask: Can you send a short mutual action plan (owner, deliverable, ETA) and confirm which Redwood features you'll exercise (streaming, function calls, quantized variants)? Also confirm whether SDK swap will require code changes on our side or can be a config-level switch.

Thanks — Josh

--
Josh Park
Head of AI Product, Stellar Media
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Park <josh@stellarmedia.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's migration discovery

Josh — thanks for the clear notes. Short internal + external plan below. I'm attaching an interop checklist and a small prompt sample for the diff run.

External recap (what we'll validate)
- API parity: endpoints will accept OpenAI-compatible payloads (messages, functions, streaming + SSE frames). We'll report mapping gaps.
- Prompt diff: we'll run your 50 canonical prompts (sanitized) through our OpenAI-compat layer and your current hyperscaler model and provide token-by-token diffs and example regressions.
- Streaming: we'll run a streaming smoke test using your UI sample to reproduce chunking and field ordering.
- Perf: p50/p95/p99 for a burst of 200 concurrent short sessions; we'll also capture cold-start behavior.

Mutual action plan (owners & ETA)
- Day 0 (today): exchange sanitized prompt set + representative client SDK versions (ACTION: Josh)
- Day 1-3: API surface compatibility checklist + smoke tests (OWNER: Aditya Rao; ETA: 72h) — deliverable: checklist + mapping doc + any missing param translations
- Day 4-7: Prompt diff runs + qualitative regression report (OWNER: Marissa Cole; ETA: 7d) — deliverable: prompt-diff-sample.txt + summary sheet
- Day 8-12: Streaming + latency tail tests (OWNER: Aditya Rao; ETA: 12d) — deliverable: perf report with traces and suggested mitigations
- Day 13-14: Joint readout and decision rubric (OWNER: Grace O'Connor; ETA: 14d)

SDK swap note: For most customers we support a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint that requires minimal client change (endpoint URL + key). There are edge cases (stream framing differences, function call encodings) that may need a single-line change or helper shim — Aditya will flag specifics in the API mapping doc.

Attachments: interop-checklist.xlsx, prompt-diff-sample.txt

If that plan looks workable I'll schedule the technical deep-dive (30-45m) for Monday or Tuesday next week.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Migration interoperability signals & next test plan

Quick technical notes from my side — I'll own the API parity and perf runs. A few things to call out so we scope correctly: 

- Streaming: Redwood's SSE frame boundaries include metadata frames for partial function-call tokens; we'll capture that in the smoke test. Your UI may need to ignore empty meta frames (1-line shim) if it assumes all frames are text.
- Functions: we support positional vs named argument encodings; we'll verify schema round-trip for your top 12 functions.
- KV cache/prefix: Redwood's prefix caching preserves role tags but our stop-token handling differs under early-termination; prompt diffs will surface regressions.
- Quantized variants: if you test q4/q5 variants we'll record subtle tokenization-induced output shifts — we'll include a delta column in the report.

I'll drop a stub harness (api-diff-script.sh) and the mapping checklist into the shared drive by EOD. Plan to run initial smoke tests against a dedicated POC instance so results aren't impacted by multi-tenant burst noise.

Aditya
Principal, Inference Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Josh Park <josh@stellarmedia.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Zhao <anita@stellarmedia.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Migration interoperability signals & next test plan

This looks great — thanks Grace and team. We will:
- Share the sanitized prompt set and sample UI harness by tomorrow morning.
- Book the Monday technical deep-dive (slot confirmed 10:00am PT).

Also, putting a quick note: Stellar Media will prioritize the streaming behavior and function-call parity — if those check out we can fast-track a small paid POC.

Josh

Quoted/forwarded content preserved where applicable.
